question: Was B1.3 v2 built on the authoritative varṇa lexicon, and does the bridge pool it WAS built on faithfully represent it?

provenance.bridge_pool_qualification: FALLBACK_QUALIFIED (generated under weaker LOCAL lexical fallback; real embedding gate BLOCKED_DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE)

pole_direction_check: PRESERVED across all 34 consonants — no binding/liberating SWAP (2 heuristic flip-flags were dda=false-positive and ha=construct-reframe, not swaps)
objects_affected: 28 of 53 primary concrete objects route through >=1 construct-drifted varṇa (ca/va/ha/ra/sa)

comparison.bp_binding: hope as grasping / clinging to a specific outcome
comparison.bp_liberating: forward-orientation held without attachment to the outcome

decision_rationale: The bridge pool is self-labeled FALLBACK_QUALIFIED and derives from an experimental draft, not the authoritative lexicon; an authoritative lexicon exists; 5 varṇas show genuine construct drift touching 28/53 objects. Freezing the primary evidence line on a fallback source when an authoritative source is available is not defensible. NOTE: pole direction is intact, so the current study is not wrong-direction, and rebuild is UNLIKELY to change the outcome (semantic baseline still names object-function; prior still low) — rebuild is about using the correct source, not improving A_real odds.
